trial_court: XV Additional District & Sessions Judge-cum-II Additional Family Court, Kukatpally at Miyapur (F.C.O.P.No.503 of 2013)
case_name: J.Shyam Babu vs J. Rajini Kumari

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: husband, he has filed FCOP No.503 of 2013 against his wife

facts_of_case: The husband obtained ex-parte divorce dissolving the marriage dated 09.05.1997. The wife came to know about the ex-parte decree and filed applications in I.A.No.601 of 2017 under Section 5 of Limitation Act to condone the delay of 12 days, and in I.A.No.602 of 2017 under Order IX, Rule 13 read with Section 151 of CPC to set aside the ex-parte decree.

legal_principles.principle: When a spouse has remarried after expiry of appeal time, filing of application by the first wife or husband to set aside the ex-parte decree and allowing the same may defeat the intention of the legislature to settle the rights of the parties permanently after divorce at shortest period of time.
legal_principles.held: The gist of the ratio laid in the above decisions is that when spouse has remarried after expiry of appeal time, filing of application by the first wife or husband, to set aside the ex-parte decree and allowing the same may defeat the intention of the legislature to settle the rights of the parties permanently after divorce at shortest period of time.
cited_cases: Dr.Lokeshwari Vs. Dr.Srinivasa Rao, (Year) X SCC Y
A.Raja Sundari Vs. Suresh Kumar, (Year) X SCC Y
Vijayalakshmi Vs. Kannappan, (Year) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: The approach of the Court while dealing with applications under Order IX Rule 13 C.P.C. would be liberal and elastic rather than narrow and pedantic.
legal_principles.held: Approach of the Court while dealing with such an application under Order IX Rule 13 C.P.C. would be liberal and elastic rather than narrow and pedantic.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order IX, Rule 13
cited_cases: Parimal v. Veena @ Bharti, (Year) X SCC Y

outcome.final_order: The trial Court set aside the ex-parte divorce order dated 09.03.2017 by condoning 12 days of delay.
